source_metadata.citation: Steinhagen, S. et al. Quantification of Degradation Products Formed during Heat Sterilization of Glucose Solutions by LC-MS/MS: Impact of Autoclaving Temperature and Duration on Degradation. Pharmaceuticals 2021, 14 (11), 1121.
source_metadata.notes: MAILLARD-PATH HOLD-OUT (Wave U, 2026-08-27). Never use for calibration, refitting, or any promotion decision.

content_verification.quoted_method: Abstract/Methods: 'Glucose solutions (10%, w/v) were autoclaved at 111 degC, 116 degC, and 121 degC for different durations. The GDPs glyoxal, methylglyoxal, glucosone, 3-deoxyglucosone/3-deoxygalactosone, 3,4-dideoxyglucosone-3-ene, and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural were quantified after derivatization with o-phenylenediamine by an optimized LC-MS/MS method. For all GDPs, the limit of detection was <0.078 ug/mL, and the limit of quantification was <0.236 ug/mL.' Table 1 gives F0 = 18 min for the 121 degC scheme-A run; at 121 degC F0 is numerically the hold time (the F0 reference temperature is 121.1 degC), which is why ONLY the 121 degC row is ingested - at 111 and 116 degC the paper's F0 and its actual hold time are not the same number and the paper does not print the latter unambiguously.
content_verification.quoted_table: 'Table 4. Concentrations of GDPs in 10% (w/v) glucose solution in PP bottles autoclaved according to scheme A (n = 27).' Column headers as printed include '5-HMF [ug/mL] +/- SD'. Scheme A rows: 111: GO 4.4+/-2.7, MGO 3.0+/-0.3, 2-KDG 5.9+/-2.2, 3-DG/3-DGal 56.0+/-10.2, 3,4-DGE 59.6+/-14.5, 5-HMF 81.9+/-29.5; 116: ... 5-HMF 31.6+/-0.5; 121: GO 5.6+/-1.3, MGO 2.6+/-0.2, 2-KDG 7.5+/-1.4, 3-DG/3-DGal 52.2+/-4.0, 3,4-DGE 55.5+/-1.7, 5-HMF 17.4+/-3.9.' Table 3 gives the MEASURED pH of the 10% glucose solution after scheme-A autoclaving at 121 degC as 4.36 +/- 0.0, and the non-autoclaved reference (Table 6) has 5-HMF 0.1 +/- 0.0 ug/mL.
content_verification.quantification_verdict: ADMISSIBLE. LC-MS/MS against calibration curves over 0.5-100 ug/mL with R2 >= 0.993, LOD < 0.078 ug/mL. Absolute, with the basis (ug per mL of solution) printed in the column header.

why_this_point_exists: This is deliberately a SUGAR-ONLY system: no amino acid, so it is caramelization rather than the Maillard reaction. It is in the hold-out because the repository ships a benchmark family literally named 'carbohydrate_pyrolysis_and_caramelization', and because a probe at HEAD 12f43dd showed the free-precursor engine returns EXACTLY ZERO for glucose with no amino-acid partner. A structural zero against a 17,400 ppb measurement is a scope limit worth freezing, and it is the kind of thing a fold-error median silently hides.

precursor_concentration_provenance.derivation: 10% (w/v) glucose = 100 g/L / 180.16 g/mol = 555.1 mM. Rounded to 555.0 mM.
precursor_concentration_provenance.residual_caveats: pH 4.36 is the value MEASURED after autoclaving (Table 3), not before; the paper reports 4.98 for the non-autoclaved solution. The post-autoclave value is used because it is the one the paper attaches to the scored run, and this is stated rather than silently chosen.

buffer.provenance_note: Steinhagen et al. 2021, Pharmaceuticals 14(11):1121. SOURCE PAPER NOT ON DISK and the repo carries no verbatim statement of the medium beyond '10% (w/v) glucose solution ... autoclaved at 111, 116, and 121 degC'. An unbuffered infusion solution is the LIKELY reading and it is exactly the reading this field refuses to record, because likely is not stated. ph_disagreement, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT BREAKS THE SCALE CONVENTION: conditions.ph = 4.36 is the pH measured AFTER autoclaving (the source's Table 3). The initial / non-autoclaved value is 4.98 (Table 6). Every other bundle's pH is an INITIAL bench reading, so this one is on a different scale from all twenty others -- which is why initial_ph_scale is recorded here as 'at_temperature' rather than 'bench_cooled'. The bundle discloses the choice honestly but a model that treats 4.36 as an initial condition is being handed the answer to part of its own trajectory. Reported, not edited.
buffer.ph_disagreement: conditions.ph = 4.36 is the POST-autoclave measurement; the initial value is 4.98. This bundle's pH is on a different scale from the other twenty.

5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF).target_quote: Table 4, Scheme A, 121 degC row: '5-HMF [ug/mL] +/- SD ... 17.4 +/- 3.9'.
5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF).molar_basis: ug per mL of the 10% (w/v) glucose solution, i.e. 17.4 ug/mL = 17400 ug/L = 17400 ppb. Pure decimal rescaling of the printed unit; no basis is assumed.
